lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Say what you have, what is there, what you need and what you want
readingEnglish: There's a problem on the jobsite.
There's no water and it's very hot.
I'm thirsty and I want cold water.
I have the hard hat and the gloves, but I need a tool.
I need more nails for the shingles.
There's material on the truck and debris on the ground.
We have to sweep with the broom and cover the roof with the tarp.
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Tell the crew lead what you have, what you need, and what is missing on the roof.
lessons.titleEnglish: Have, There Is, Need and Want

verbEnglish.exampleEnglish: I have the hard hat and the gloves, but I need a tool.
I need more nails for the shingles.

words.en: You have to wear the harness.

lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Talk about plans, actions and what you can do
readingEnglish: Today we're going to a new house.
We get to the jobsite early in the truck.
Now I'm going to go up on the roof.
It's hot, so we work fast.
Can you help me with the ladder?
After that we do the cleanup.
Tomorrow we're going to start another roof.
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Explain your plan for today on the jobsite and ask a crew member if they can help you.

verbEnglish.exampleEnglish: Now I'm going to go up on the roof.
After that we do the cleanup.
Can you help me with the ladder?

lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Say what you and the crew do every day with regular verbs
readingEnglish: I work on roofs five days a week.
The crew gets to the jobsite at six in the morning.
We go up at seven.
My coworker cuts the shingles and I nail.
We eat lunch at twelve.
In the afternoon, the crew brings down the old material.
We clean up at the end of the day.
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Describe a normal workday: when the crew arrives, what you do in the morning and afternoon.

verbEnglish.exampleEnglish: I work on roofs five days a week.
We clean up at the end of the day.

words.en: We clean up at the end.
